title: What is LTV? Customer Lifetime Value Formula & Benchmarks
meta_description: LTV is the revenue one customer returns before leaving. The formula, the realised figures for AI and non-AI apps, and why a modelled LTV flatters itself.

visuals.alt: Six LTV reference points: realised year-one LTV for AI and non-AI apps, the highest-LTV paywall configuration, the monthly retention curve, annual renewal by category, typical monthly churn, and the lift from adding a trial to an annual plan, each row carrying its source and verification date
visuals.caption: Realised LTV reference points, each row sourced. Verified 30 September 2026.

faq.a: ARPU divided by churn rate gives the simple version. It assumes a constant churn rate, which no real cohort has, so it overstates. Summing the actual revenue of a closed cohort is slower and correct.

faq.q: What is a good LTV for a subscription app?
faq.a: Realised year-one LTV runs at a $21.37 median, about ₹2,049, for non-AI apps and $30.16, about ₹2,892, for AI apps. Judge yours against your own category and your own paywall shape, not against the overall figure.

faq.q: Should LTV use revenue or gross profit?
faq.a: Gross profit, if you are comparing it against CAC. Store commission, payment fees and support cost all sit between the revenue line and the money that pays back acquisition. Revenue-based LTV flatters every ratio it touches.

unique_value_statement: Separates realised LTV from modelled LTV and gives the published realised figures for both AI and non-AI apps, where the ranking pages give only the ARPU-over-churn formula and no realised number to check it against.
